summary: Cleveland must win with a bullpen game on tired arms after a no-off-day flight; Peralta (0.79 postseason ERA) starts for TB. Most likely winner: Tampa Bay Rays ML.

extra_legs.note: Peralta faces a Cleveland bullpen game thrown by arms working back-to-back after a no-off-day flight.
Under 6.5 has hit in 8 of 11 meetings this year and Cleveland has 4 runs in two games.
All three Rays wins this series came by 2+ runs, and Cleveland's lesser relievers may pitch big innings.
Peralta blanked Cleveland for six innings in Game 2, and the Guardians scored once in two of five games.

extra_legs.book: StatMuse odds page (DK +105 via Sportsbook Review, +118 via Tony's Picks)
extra_legs.status: Confirmed probable (MLB StatsAPI, ESPN); threw 9 pitches in relief on 10/17, Cash says no effect
extra_legs.note: Peralta got 15+ outs in his last six regular-season starts and 18 in Game 2, and TB's top relievers are worn.
Peralta struck out six Guardians in Game 2, but he averages 4.3 strikeouts a start for Tampa Bay.

research:
SOURCES (deep pass, 25 web searches plus MLB StatsAPI boxscores/stats and the ESPN summary API; WebFetch fails DNS and most news sites are proxy-blocked, so article quotes come from search snippets): MLB.com (Game 6 FAQ/storylines), ESPN (G5 story, 'facing elimination' story, pickcenter, BPI), Baseball Prospectus G6 preview, Yahoo/SI FanNation, theScore, NBC Sports/Rotowire, VSiN, Sportsbook Review, Bettor's Insider (pick + SGP), Lineups.com, Fanatics Sportsbook blog, DK Network, FanDuel Research, StatMuse, Tony's Picks, SportBook.ag, Guardians Nation, thecapper.io, Ballpark Pal.
1) SERIES: TB leads 3-2. G1 CLE 7-3 (TB), G2 TB 3-1 (TB), G3 CLE 3-2 (CLE), G4 TB 7-3 (CLE, Sat 10/17 8:08 PM), G5 TB 3-1 (CLE, Sun 10/18 5:08 PM; Rasmussen 7 IP 1 ER 6 K 95 pitches; Yandy Diaz 3 hits). G6 Mon 8:08 PM ET at the Trop, G7 Tue if needed. CLE flew Sunday night with no off day. CLE has scored 4 runs in the last two games and 15 in 5 ALCS games (3.0/G); TB 18 (3.6/G).
2) CLE STARTER DECISION: Vogt said Gavin Williams is 'not an option' and is held for G7. No starter is listed (MLB StatsAPI and ESPN blank at research time). MLB.com FAQ: bullpen game, 'RHP Slade Cecconi potentially starting things off'. Baseball Prospectus: second bullpen game in three days; Joey Cantillo most likely to give length. Several outlets: Tanner Bibee is the freshest arm (last pitched 10/8, 15 pitches, 11 days ago) and will pitch in some capacity. SportBook.ag's 'Bieber' start is stale and discounted.
3) CLE BULK OPTIONS (StatsAPI 2026): Cantillo LHP 3.62 ERA, 3.98 FIP, K 24.9%, BB 11.8%, xwOBA .306; in Sept bulk relief 15 IP 0 ER (4, 6, 5 IP); ALCS 1.2 IP 0 ER, last used 10/17 (15 pitches). Bibee RHP 4.36 ERA, 4.52 FIP, K 19.0%, BB 7.1%, xwOBA .318; 22 ER in his last 31.2 IP of the regular season. Cecconi RHP 4.91 ERA, 4.55 FIP, K 18.8%, xwOBA .333; 22 pitches 10/17. Griffin LHP 44 pitches 10/17 (3.2 IP), possible only in short relief.
4) PERALTA (TB, RHP): 2026 32 GS, 169.0 IP, 4.42 ERA, 1.33 WHIP, K 21.4% (156/730), BB 8.6%, FIP 4.28, xFIP 4.37, xwOBA .300 (Mets-era xERA 3.83 per first pass). With TB: 10 GS, 55.1 IP, 3.25 ERA, 1.01 WHIP, K 19.7%, BB 6.9%, FIP 3.93, 4.3 K and 16.6 outs per start. Last six regular-season starts 81, 74, 92, 86, 97, 93 pitches, all 15+ outs. Postseason: ALDS 4.2 IP/66 pitches; ALCS G2 vs CLE 6.0 IP 0 R 4 H 6 K 2 BB 99 pitches (fastball to 99.4); 9 pitches in relief 10/17 (two days before this start; Cash and Peralta said it changes nothing). Postseason ERA 0.79.
5) BULLPEN FATIGUE (StatsAPI boxscores; G4 10/17, G5 10/18, G6 10/19). CLE: Armstrong 13+13 and Herrin 14+18 would be pitching a 3rd straight day; Smith (22 pitches, 1.1 IP), Gaddis (19, 1.2 IP) and Sabrowski (18, 1.2 IP) pitched G5 and would go back-to-back; Cecconi 22, Espino 22, Festa 21, Cantillo 15, Griffin 44 all pitched G4 (one day of rest); Messick 57 in G5 (out); Bibee rested 11 days. Vogt used Smith down two runs in the 8th of G5. TB: Baker (closer) 12+14 and Booser 4+10 would be a 3rd straight day; Wells 5 in G5 (back-to-back); Seymour 29 in G4 (4th outing of the series) and Kelly 16 in G4 have one day of rest; Matz (last 10/15), Sulser (G1), Jax (G3 starter, 67 pitches 10/15) and Hopkins are fresh. TB pen ERA this series is 4.60 per SI. Both late-inning groups are worn, which argues for a longer Peralta leash.
6) LINEUPS AND SPLITS (not posted yet; G5 lineups): CLE Kwan CF, J. Ramirez 3B (7 hits in series), DeLauter RF, Adell DH, Lowe 1B, Bazzana 2B, Bailey C, A. Martinez LF, Rocchio SS (Halpin bench). TB Diaz DH, Aranda 1B, Caminero 3B, Mullins, Mesa Jr. RF, DeLuca CF, Simpson LF, Palacios/Williamson, Hicks C, Walls SS. Diaz and Caminero were pinch-run for in the 9th of G5 (no injury reported); Diaz publicly guaranteed 'it all ends tomorrow'. CLE 2026: .706 OPS vs RHP (K 20.6%), .675 vs LHP, .687 on the road. TB: .752 OPS vs RHP, .679 vs LHP, .748 at home vs .709 away. CLE's bulk options are mostly RHP (Bibee, Cecconi), which plays into TB's better split; Cantillo (LHP) is the exception.
7) INJURIES (ESPN): TB Lux, Uceta, Heasley, Melton (60-day IL), McClanahan out (forearm). CLE Hoskins (10-day, back), Holderman (15-day, wrist), Walters out (elbow). No new G6 injury news found.
8) PARK: Tropicana Field, indoors (no weather). thecapper/Savant-based run index 94, HR index 103; other sources 0.95-0.97 runs, 0.92-0.93 HR. Pitcher-friendly overall. ESPN notes the right-field porch no longer helps LHB like Aranda.
9) MANAGERS: Cash pulls starters before a 3rd time through the order (2020 WS G6 Snell precedent); in this series his starters went 18, 18, 12, 16, 21 outs. Vogt runs openers and bulk relievers aggressively and pulled Messick after 2 IP/57 pitches in G5, and starters in ALCS have gone 12, 15, 15, 6 outs for CLE.
10) ELIMINATION HISTORY: CLE won three straight elimination games in the ALDS vs CHW after trailing 0-2 (11th team ever to do so). Teams down 3-2 in the ALCS have come back 7 of 23 times (ESPN/Yahoo), though the last two did (TEX 2023, TOR 2025). TB went 5-1 vs CLE in the regular season (3-0 at the Trop in July, including a 1-0 one-hitter). CLE eliminated TB in the 2022 Wild Card (15-inning walk-off).
11) MARKET AND MOVEMENT: ESPN pickcenter (DraftKings): ML opened TB -130 / CLE +108, now TB -149 / CLE +123; DK Network opener -137/+113; Bettor's Insider Sunday night DK -143/+119. Run line TB -1.5 opened +178, now +155 (CLE +1.5 -188). Total 6.5 flat (o-114/u-106 to o-114/u-105). Fanatics: TB -145/CLE +120, TB -1.5 +155/CLE +1.5 -190, o6.5 -115/u6.5 -105. SI: TB -147, run line +161/-196, total o-114/u-106. DocSports outlier total 7 (CLE +113/TB -136). Money has come in on TB as the CLE bullpen-game news firmed. No-vig: TB ML 0.569, Under 6.5 0.49, TB -1.5 0.375. CLE team total 2.5 o-140/u+110 (ESPN Bet via Bettor's Insider), no-vig under 0.449. Peralta K 4.5: FanDuel o+126/u-162, StatMuse o+125/u-135, VSiN o+119. Peralta outs 14.5: StatMuse o+125/u-133, DK o+105 (SBR), Tony's Picks o+118.
12) EXPERT PICKS: Bettor's Insider: Rays ML (cites ESPN model 59.5%), plus SGP Under 6.5 + CLE team total u2.5 + Diaz hit. Lineups.com: Under 6.5 (-108 DK), Rays 5-1. VSiN: Peralta o4.5 K (+119) and Rays -1.5 (+161). Sportsbook Review: Rays ML -138, Peralta o14.5 outs (+105 DK), Diaz HR +700. Tony's Picks: Peralta o14.5 outs (+118). Akron Beacon Journal panel (Yahoo): Rays 5-3. SportBook.ag: Under 7.5, CLE 3-2 (stale pitcher names, weak). SI prop: Jose Ramirez. ESPN Matchup Predictor: TB 55.5%. Consensus: Rays side, Under, Peralta length.
13) TOTALS HISTORY: ALCS totals 10, 4, 5, 10, 4 (Under 6.5 3 of 5); 2026 regular-season meetings 5, 1, 4, 14, 3, 1. Under 6.5 has hit in 8 of 11 TB-CLE games this year. Against that, CLE is running out tired relievers and a lesser bulk arm at a lineup that hits RHP well at home.
LEAN: Rays ML is the most likely winner (fair 0.57; Peralta vs a third-string CLE bullpen game, CLE late arms on back-to-back or 3rd straight days, travel with no off day). The strongest edge is Peralta o14.5 outs: he went 15+ outs in all six of his last regular-season starts and 18 in G2, and TB's own late relievers (Baker, Booser 3rd straight day; Seymour heavily used) give Cash a reason to ride him. The total is near fair; Under 6.5 is a small lean only.
game5_context: Game 5 (10/18): Rays 3, Guardians 1, so TB leads 3-2. Rasmussen 7 IP, 6 K, 1 ER, 95 pitches. TB pen light: Booser 10 pitches, Wells 5, Baker 14. CLE used six arms: Messick 2 IP, 57 pitches (quick hook); Herrin 18, Armstrong 13, Sabrowski 18, Gaddis 19, Cade Smith 22, so CLE's top relievers worked on back-to-back days if Game 6 is Monday.
